ravi: FYI canary v3.4.2 at 25% in us-west2 showing p95 creeping up, started ~7m ago :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: rollout: v3.4.2 -> 25% us-west2. metrics snapshot: p95=680ms (baseline 320ms), errors=0.06%. autorevert rule p95>700ms sustained 5m. breach timer started 2m ago.
emily: only on the /chat-stream route? looks concentrated on long seq requests.
ops-marta: recommend pin+manual hold and try a kv-cache warmup probe on the canary pods before rollback. low blast radius so manual triage preferred.
ravi: pinning at 25% and applying manual hold now. deploy-bot: traffic pinned at 25% by ravi; autopilot rollback suppressed.
sre-jorge: plan: 1) run kv-cache warmup script on canary pod pair, 2) restart one worker in the pair, 3) monitor p95 for 8m. rollback to v3.4.1 if p95 >=650ms sustained 6m.
pm-lee: customer blurb draft: "Paused canary for v3.4.2 due to increased latency for a subset of streamed requests. We're investigating and will either resume or roll back. No customer-facing errors observed." ops-marta ok to send?
ops-marta: send and tag #support-watch.
sre-jorge: warming cache on pod-03/04 now. snippet: `curl -s http://pod-03/internal/warm_kv?keys=top1000`
sre-jorge: after warm + restart pod-04 p95 dropped to 340ms; cluster p95 360ms. keeping hold for 10m. if it regresses above 650ms for 6m we execute rollback to v3.4.1 (build 20260615.3).
ravi: logging decision: reason=canary-p95-drift-stream-route, action=manual-hold+kv-warmup+restart, rollback-if=6m sustained >650ms, rollback-target=v3.4.1. will update thread in 10m. :hourglass:
